commentary_title: VLCC utilisation strengthened despite improving vessel availability,
commentary_summary: VLCC utilisation strengthened to 91.9% during the week, remaining above the long-term equilibrium level despite signs of rising vessel availability. A modest recovery in the tonne-mile index and a higher share of laden vessels in the East indicate that crude trade demand remained sufficiently resilient to absorb available tonnage and support overall fleet employment. | East of Suez continued to underpin market fundamentals, although signs of easing tightness emerged. The proportion of laden vessels increased, reflecting healthy cargo activity, but underway tonnage fell sharply while anchored tonnage rose substantially. This suggests that vessel availability around major Middle East loading areas is rebuilding as cargo growth struggles to keep pace with fleet positioning. | Congestion across major Asian discharge hubs eased further, particularly in China. Laden tonnage at anchor in China declined sharply while Indian discharge-side congestion remained well below earlier peaks. The reduction in waiting times removed an important supply constraint and contributed to the recovery in effective fleet productivity observed across the VLCC market.
